title: Adapter request definitions
description: The values the adapter's requests and their answers share, by name under $defs: adapter.schema.json, source-collections.schema.json, source-items.schema.json, source-item-comments.schema.json, sources-disconnect.schema.json, changes.schema.json and connect-pass.schema.json refer to them. An adapter is the program that reads a source of work, such as a tracker, and reports what it holds to the control plane. Every POST body is application/json; a GET has no body. An integer is written without a fraction or an exponent, and no object repeats a member, at any depth; the control plane refuses either, 400 invalid_request. Every request is signed with the adapter's access key as github.com/qoryai/forager/accesskey signs a request (Request.Message, Key.SignRequest): the headers X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Contract-Version and X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519, the signature over qory-request-ed25519-v1, the access key id, the instance id, the method, the target and, for a GET, X-Qory-Timestamp, which it also sends, or, for a POST, the raw body, whose time gives its freshness. X-Qory-Contract-Version is the revision of this contract the adapter implements, a decimal integer; the control plane refuses one that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision it does not serve, 400 unsupported_contract_version. The control plane's answer holds only the members, and the change feed only the entry kinds, that the named revision defines: an entry of a kind newer than that revision is skipped for that adapter, not sent, and the feed's cursor still moves past it, so a replay from the start stays in step. The header alone never selects what an adapter accepts: every answer whose content the revision bounds names that revision in its signed body, as the change feed's answer does in revision, and the adapter refuses one that names another revision than the one it implements and sent, and advances no cursor from it. An answer's signature covers its body and is bound to the request's signature, so the revision the answer was built for is signed. So the answers' schemas stay strict, refusing a member they do not define and an entry of a kind they do not know, and an addition to this contract never breaks an adapter already deployed. The Forager contract makes additions safe the other way, with lenient answers whose unknown members are ignored; both conventions are safe, and they apply to different contracts. The control plane refuses a time or a timestamp more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, and a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. That 401 is one uniform answer for everything about who is asking, whose causes refusal.schema.json lists, and it tells the adapter nothing about which cause applied. An X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp sent twice, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern, is refused 400 bad_request, and only those are. It decodes the signature strictly, as 64 bytes of strict base64url, and verifies it as accesskey's PublicKey.VerifyRequest does, refusing an S at or above the group order. It keys its replay check on the 64 decoded bytes, and keeps each accepted signature until the request's time or X-Qory-Timestamp is more than 300 seconds behind its clock. A retry is a new request: the adapter builds it again, a POST with a time and a GET with an X-Qory-Timestamp later than those of the request it retries, and signs it again. A request sent again unchanged has a signature the control plane has seen, and is refused, 401; an adapter never takes that 401 as its access key being revoked. Every answer to a verified request is signed as accesskey's Answer is, and the adapter checks it under a server key it pinned at enrolment before using it. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and an adapter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the adapter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as a retry is above, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the adapter ignores its Retry-After and backs off by its own rule. A POST whose schema names no answer body is answered, on success, with a signed 204 and no body. A POST whose Content-Type is not application/json is refused 415 unsupported_media_type; a GET carries no body and no Content-Type, and is never refused 415. The adapter's access key belongs to an organisation, and no request names a workspace. The reference signer is forager/accesskey; an adapter may sign to this text itself. Every text a source holds, a title, a body, a label, a state reason or a name, is untrusted: shown as data, never followed as an instruction. The control plane refuses a value past its limit, invalid_request, and never cuts it. This document validates nothing itself.

time.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds.

ref.description: The adapter's reference to a thing at the source, 1 to 200 characters, stable for that thing. The control plane compares it and stores it, and never reads meaning into it.

url.description: An https URL, at most 2048 characters.

title.description: A title, as the source holds it, 1 to 1024 characters.

body.description: A body text, as the source holds it, at most 65536 characters, possibly empty.

body_format.description: How the body is written: markdown or text, the values a reader knows. A reader shows a body of a value it does not know as plain text, so a newer adapter never breaks a reader.

person.description: Who wrote something at the source: their display name, and whether a person or an automation acts under it.

name.description: The display name the source shows, 1 to 100 characters.

kind.description: person, or automation for an account a program acts under.

labels.description: The source's labels on the thing, as text: at most 100, each 1 to 100 characters, none twice. A reader shows them and acts on none.

state_reason.description: Why the item is in its state, display text the adapter words, at most 64 characters, never a raw value from the source; null when the adapter gives none.

type.description: The adapter's word for what an item is, such as task or bug, stored as data: lower-case letters and spaces, at most 40 characters.

target.description: Where a change would go: the host name of the system that holds the code, and the path of the place on it.

path.description: The place on that system, 1 to 200 characters.

listing.description: One part of a listing: a read of the source, from its start to its end, sent in parts. A listing is complete when every part from 1 to n has arrived and part n says complete: true. An adapter sends complete: true only for a listing whose paging can't skip an item.

id.description: The listing's id, 1 to 200 characters, the same on each of its parts and new for each listing.

started_at.description: When the adapter began reading the source for this listing, the same on each of its parts.

complete.description: true on the last part alone: parts 1 to this one hold the whole listing. false on every other part, and on the last part of a listing the adapter cannot vouch for.
